overview.purpose: How strong is the case that [technology family] could improve AI alignment, preserve broadly distributed human agency, or both; through which deployment scenarios; and under what conditions? Families: WBE, BCI, neuromorphic AI.
principles: 1. Unit of analysis = technology family. Each entry records the scenario(s) it addresses; transfer to another scenario requires a recorded justification.
2. Each causal link is a separate claim (evidence for one link is never evidence for the chain).
3. Absence of evidence is not contrary evidence ('Search incomplete' until a documented search).
4. Source quality is coded independently of direction; quality sets update size.
5. Incremental updates: a new source changes a rating only if the accumulated evidence justifies it.
6. Severity, likelihood and confidence are never combined.
7. Definitions and update rules are fixed per version; changes need a version increment.
update_protocol: 1. Add a row to 3 Sources and code it in 3a Source Quality.
2. Extract each relevant claim as one 0 Evidence Register row: scenario(s), stage, directness, role and basis.
3. Map each entry to link, milestone, risk or checklist IDs (column E).
4. Recompute the evidence status of mapped items with the status rule (Codebook); check the 'Strongest objection' column in 2 Theory of Change for any new answer or objection.

5. Decide whether the accumulated evidence changes a rating or confidence (rating rules in Codebook). Update the rating and reason on the judgment tab and the 'Ratings it feeds' column of the Evidence Register. Synopsis updates itself.

milestone_categories.label: Technical capability
milestone_categories.question: Can the relevant components be built and operated? Counts as evidence: demonstrated progress on a named prerequisite, with scale stated. Does not count: general optimism; progress not tied to a named prerequisite; results from another technology family without a stated reason they transfer.

milestone_categories.label: High-level fidelity
milestone_categories.question: Does the system reproduce specified properties of the original (person, signal or mechanism) accurately enough for the use? Counts as evidence: a system reproducing a listed property, with a stated test. Does not count: technical capability alone; unspecified 'accuracy'; resemblance without a test.

milestone_categories.label: Reliability and robustness
milestone_categories.question: Does performance hold across time, people, conditions and distribution shift? Counts as evidence: replicated or long-term results; tests across people or tasks. Does not count: single-condition demonstrations.

milestone_categories.label: Safety and welfare assurance
milestone_categories.question: Can harms to users, third parties or artificial minds be detected and prevented? Counts as evidence: validated safety protocols, welfare-monitoring methods or security countermeasures. Does not count: statements that safety matters.

milestone_categories.label: Scalable manufacture, compute and data
milestone_categories.question: Can inputs be supplied at the required scale? Counts as evidence: resource-scaling data or projections with stated assumptions. Does not count: unquantified statements.

milestone_categories.label: Economic viability
milestone_categories.question: Are scanning, compute, storage, maintenance and infrastructure costs practical at the scale needed for the claimed benefit? Counts as evidence: cost data, compute requirements, resource scaling, infrastructure requirements, or an economic model. Does not count: statements that costs will fall; unquantified 'low cost'.

milestone_categories.label: Legal and regulatory permission
milestone_categories.question: Is the use legally permitted? Counts as evidence: statutes, regulatory decisions, formal guidance. Does not count: commentary on what the law should be.

milestone_categories.label: Institutional capacity and legitimacy
milestone_categories.question: Can institutions govern it with public acceptance? Counts as evidence: institutional analyses; public-attitude data. Does not count: claims of acceptance without data.

milestone_categories.label: Equitable or broad access (if claimed)
milestone_categories.question: Is access broad and meaningful? Applies only where a source claims broad benefit. Counts as evidence: access, pricing or distribution data. Does not count: assertions.

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Five prerequisites: (P1) whole-brain scanning of a human brain; (P2) models turning structure into dynamics; (P3) compute and storage to run in real time; (P4) a validation method; (P5) body and environment input/output. Met = all five at the scale the intended use needs. Partly = at least one at mammalian whole-brain scale.
milestone_assessments.evidence: E037, E043, E065 (components demonstrated; whole brain argued)
milestone_assessments.bottleneck: P2 turning a connectome into a runnable model; P1 scanning throughput
milestone_assessments.timing: No date in any source; signals point to a long horizon (S13 'many years out'; S21 expects other AI first)
milestone_assessments.note: Best result: 1 mm³ of human cortex (S16), about a millionth of the brain. Evidence on parts of the brain does not meet the whole-emulation criterion.

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Three prerequisites: recording the target signal where it is used; real-time decoding; closed-loop link to AI training or oversight. Met = all three with at least 10 participants in at least 2 independent groups.
milestone_assessments.bottleneck: Recording evaluative signals in realistic settings; closed-loop link to AI training
milestone_assessments.timing: Met now at laboratory scale (S24, S26)
milestone_assessments.note: Decoding replicated in lab tasks (S26, S27); closed-loop training only in simple tasks (S24, S25). Clinical implants (S16) are therapy evidence, not alignment evidence.

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: As above, shown in healthy users for oversight or enhancement.
milestone_assessments.bottleneck: No bandwidth or enhancement demonstration in healthy users
milestone_assessments.note: S09 likely relevant but not accessible.

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Chip built and benchmarked on a standard workload, replicated by at least 2 groups.
milestone_assessments.bottleneck: Controlling plasticity in self-assembled hardware (S06)

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Architecture with specified motivational subsystems implemented and run, replicated by at least 2 groups.

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Properties by use. Overseer: oversight judgement, domain knowledge, error detection. Researcher: reasoning, expertise, research motivation. General-purpose AI: values, preferences, decision-making. Institutional: decision judgement. Labour: task competence, personality, memory. Threshold (draft): on pre-registered held-out tasks the emulation is statistically indistinguishable from the original person, and drifts no more than the person's own test-retest variation.
milestone_assessments.bottleneck: No method to validate reproduced properties (S17); no theory of simulation stability (S13)

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Threshold (draft): single-trial decoding agrees with the person's intent at least as well as their explicit feedback does, on new participants.

milestone_assessments.success_criterion: Brain-inspired AGI: the specified motivational mechanism produces its predicted behaviour in tests. Neural-data models (draft): model-brain similarity at least equal to similarity between human subjects.

links.claim: Prerequisite: a single whole human emulation can be built and run.
links.assumption: Scanning, functional modelling and compute prerequisites all met (see WBE-M1).

links.claim: Fidelity: the emulation reproduces the original person's oversight-relevant properties (judgement of acceptable vs unacceptable AI behaviour, domain knowledge, error detection) to the high-level fidelity threshold.
links.assumption: A validation protocol for oversight-relevant judgement exists and is passed.
links.objection: Inherited values would include aggression, power-seeking and other human failings (E039). Not answered.

links.claim: Stability: those properties persist under copying, acceleration, long subjective runtime and a changed (virtual) environment.
links.assumption: No value or judgement drift under altered timescale, embodiment or isolation.
links.objection: Values drift under acceleration, copying, selection and long subjective runtime (E062, E091, E090). Not answered.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Oversight efficacy: a WBE overseer can detect and correct misbehaviour of an AI system MORE capable than itself.
links.assumption: Overseer is not deceived or manipulated by the supervised system; speed-up suffices to close the capability gap.
links.objection: A human-derived overseer may move the oversight problem rather than solve it. Not stated by any source; not answered.

links.claim: Comparative benefit: WBE oversight outperforms available or plausible non-WBE oversight (human + tools, AI-assisted oversight, debate, interpretability) on the same task.
links.assumption: A comparison on matched tasks exists.

links.claim: Timing: WBE overseers are available before AI systems requiring such oversight are deployed (strategic window).
links.assumption: WBE timelines shorter than timelines to AI requiring oversight.
links.objection: Competing approach: other advanced AI and conventional alignment are likely to arrive first, so the window may not exist (E038, E092, E007). Answered only by argument (S16).

links.claim: Deployment: actors deploy WBEs for oversight under conditions that preserve fidelity, stability and oversight efficacy (not repurposed for capabilities).
links.assumption: Governance controls on use of emulations.

links.claim: Prerequisite: emulations can be built and copied.
links.assumption: As WBE-O-L1 plus cheap copying.

links.claim: Fidelity: the emulation reproduces research-relevant cognition of the original (reasoning, expertise, motivation to work on alignment).
links.assumption: Research competence survives emulation; validation protocol exists.

links.claim: Stability: research motivation and values persist under acceleration, copying and long subjective time.
links.assumption: No drift in goals under altered conditions.
links.objection: Values drift under acceleration, copying, selection and long subjective runtime (E062, E091, E090). Not answered.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Throughput: running accelerated copies multiplies useful alignment-research output.
links.assumption: Alignment research is parallelisable and not bottlenecked by experiments on external systems.

links.claim: Differential: the added research capacity is directed to alignment more than to capabilities.
links.assumption: Access controls on who runs emulations and on what.

links.claim: Comparative benefit: WBE researchers outperform AI-assisted alignment research (e.g. LLM research agents) at comparable cost and time.
links.assumption: A matched comparison exists.

links.claim: Timing: WBE researchers are available within the strategic window.
links.assumption: As WBE-O-L6.
links.objection: Competing approach: other advanced AI and conventional alignment are likely to arrive first, so the window may not exist (E038, E092, E007). Answered only by argument (S16).

links.claim: Prerequisite: emulations can be built and then enhanced or modified.
links.assumption: Modification techniques exist.

links.claim: Value fidelity: the emulation inherits the original person's values and preferences, so values need not be specified separately.
links.assumption: The original's values are themselves acceptable; values are reproduced, not only behaviour.
links.objection: Inherited values would include aggression, power-seeking and other human failings (E039). Not answered.

links.claim: Stability: inherited values persist under modification, enhancement, acceleration, copying and selection pressure.
links.assumption: No value drift under any of these operations.
links.objection: Values drift under acceleration, copying, selection and long subjective runtime (E062, E091, E090). Not answered.

links.claim: Safe scaling: an enhanced or accelerated emulation remains aligned as it becomes more capable than unenhanced humans.
links.assumption: Human motivational systems remain benign at superhuman capability.

links.claim: Comparative benefit: a WBE-based system is safer than a de novo AI system of equal capability.
links.assumption: A comparison basis exists.

links.claim: Timing / differential development: WBE-based intelligence arrives before unaligned de novo AGI.
links.assumption: WBE can be accelerated and AGI timelines are not short.
links.objection: Competing approach: other advanced AI and conventional alignment are likely to arrive first, so the window may not exist (E038, E092, E007). Answered only by argument (S16).

links.claim: No capability spillover: WBE research does not accelerate unaligned AGI more than it advances aligned intelligence.
links.assumption: Neuroscience insights do not transfer to de novo AI capabilities.
links.objection: WBE research speeds up unaligned AI more than aligned intelligence (E040, E068). Answered only by argument (S16).

links.claim: Fidelity: emulations reproduce the judgement of the persons they are copied from on institutional decisions.
links.assumption: As WBE-O-L2 for decision tasks.

links.claim: Adoption: institutions give emulations a decision or advisory role.
links.assumption: Legal permission and public legitimacy are in place.

links.claim: Effect: emulation participation improves institutional decisions relative to non-WBE decision support and preserves human-derived influence.
links.assumption: Measurable decision quality; emulations represent biological constituents.

links.claim: Prerequisite: populations of emulations can be run at economic scale.
links.assumption: Technical capability and scale milestones met for populations of emulations.

links.claim: Economic viability: emulation labour is cheaper than biological human labour for a large share of tasks.
links.assumption: Compute, storage and maintenance costs per emulation-hour below wage levels.

links.claim: Ownership mechanism: the source specifies who owns scans, emulations and compute, and who receives returns (see the ownership gate).
links.assumption: Ownership arrangements are specified and enforceable.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Distribution of returns: returns from emulation labour reach biological humans broadly, not only owners of scans, emulations or compute.
links.assumption: Broad ownership or redistribution mechanism.
links.objection: Cheap copyable labour removes workers' bargaining power; only asset holders benefit, if property rights hold (E087, E089, E095). Not answered.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Bargaining power: biological humans retain economic bargaining power when emulation labour is available.
links.assumption: Biological humans have something powerful actors need.
links.objection: Cheap copyable labour removes workers' bargaining power; only asset holders benefit, if property rights hold (E087, E089, E095). Not answered.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Emulated persons' agency: emulations can own assets, refuse work, leave, or move compute provider. Reported separately; does not count as biological-human agency.
links.assumption: Legal personhood or equivalent protections.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Political influence: biological humans retain political and institutional influence alongside large emulation populations.
links.assumption: Voting / representation rules adapted.

links.claim: Comparative: outcomes for biological humans are better than under non-WBE labour-replacing AI (Intelligence Curse comparator).
links.assumption: The team agrees the Intelligence Curse comparator.

links.claim: Recording: devices capture the target signal (evaluative, error, affective, approval) at the scale and in the settings required.
links.assumption: Required resolution and coverage are specified.

links.claim: Decoding fidelity: the target signal is decoded on single trials at or above the high-level fidelity threshold.
links.assumption: Decoder generalises across people, sessions and tasks.
links.objection: Decoding is too inaccurate and person-specific; missed errors harm learning more than false alarms (E103, E106). Partly answered: pre-training across people (E107).

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Information gain: the neural signal carries alignment-relevant information not available from explicit feedback (ratings, comparisons, language).
links.assumption: Incremental validity over explicit feedback is measurable.
links.objection: Alternative explanation: gains may come from more feedback, not new information; no study compares an equal amount of explicit feedback (E099, E101, E108). Not stated by any source; not answered.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Training efficacy: agents trained with neural feedback behave closer to human intent than agents trained without it.
links.assumption: Effect replicates beyond the training task.
links.objection: Alternative explanation: gains may come from more feedback, not new information; no study compares an equal amount of explicit feedback (E099, E101, E108). Not stated by any source; not answered.

links.claim: Goodhart / manipulation robustness: optimising against neural signals does not lead the AI to exploit the signal or to manipulate the person.
links.assumption: Signals are not easily gamed; safeguards exist.
links.objection: The AI learns to trigger the signal rather than meet the person's intent. Not stated by any source; not answered.

links.claim: Frontier transfer: information gain, training efficacy and robustness hold for frontier-scale AI and open-ended tasks, not only constrained reinforcement-learning tasks.
links.assumption: Scaling of neural feedback to complex behaviours.

links.claim: Comparative benefit: neural feedback outperforms RLHF / RLAIF / other non-neuro feedback at comparable cost.
links.assumption: Matched comparison exists.
links.objection: Competing approach: resources would do more good on interpretability; the limits of feedback-based training apply to neural feedback too (E056, E109). Not answered.

links.claim: Bandwidth: BCIs increase human-AI information bandwidth or reduce latency for oversight tasks.
links.assumption: Usable output/input rates exceed conventional interfaces.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Oversight efficacy: BCI-augmented overseers detect AI failures, manipulation or deception faster or more accurately than unaided overseers.
links.assumption: Tested on oversight tasks.

links.claim: Capability gap: the advantage persists against AI systems more capable than the overseer (not a constant-factor speed-up).
links.assumption: Bandwidth gain scales with AI capability.
links.objection: BCIs give only a fixed speed-up; a scaled AI outpaces it (E049, E051). Not answered.

links.claim: Security: the interface does not give the supervised AI a channel to manipulate or take over the overseer.
links.assumption: Read-only or secured write channels.
links.objection: The interface becomes an attack channel: an AI could hijack the user or manipulate what an overseer sees (E052, E053). Answered only by argument: read-only interfaces (S14).

links.claim: Comparative benefit: outperforms non-BCI oversight tooling at comparable cost.
links.assumption: Matched comparison.
links.objection: Competing approach: resources would do more good on interpretability; the limits of feedback-based training apply to neural feedback too (E056, E109). Not answered.

links.claim: Enhancement: BCIs measurably enhance cognition in healthy users.
links.assumption: Demonstration in non-clinical users.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Research effect: enhanced humans produce better or faster alignment research; any 'merge' proposal specifies its mechanism.
links.assumption: Mechanism specified.

links.claim: Differential: enhancement benefits alignment more than capabilities research.
links.assumption: Access controls.
links.objection: Enhancement helps capability researchers equally, and an unaligned AI would want to remove merged humans (E050, E055). Not answered.

links.claim: Safety of enhanced/merged humans: enhanced or merged humans do not become a risk (malevolence, AI incentive to remove them, mental-health harm).
links.objection: Enhancement helps capability researchers equally, and an unaligned AI would want to remove merged humans (E050, E055). Not answered.

links.claim: Comparative / competitiveness: enhanced humans remain competitive with AI-only systems as AI capability grows.
links.assumption: Enhancement gains scale with AI capability.
links.objection: BCIs give only a fixed speed-up; a scaled AI outpaces it (E049, E051). Not answered.

links.claim: Broad access: enhancement is broadly accessible.
links.assumption: Pricing and distribution data.

links.claim: Ownership: productivity gains from enhancement are retained by the user (ownership gate: data, firmware, returns, exit).
links.assumption: Ownership arrangements specified.

links.claim: Disempowerment pathway: workplace neurosurveillance is technically feasible and deployed.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Disempowerment pathway: workplace use shifts bargaining power from workers to employers (monitoring, hiring/firing decisions, neurodiscrimination).
links.assumption: Workers cannot refuse without exclusion.
links.objection: Counter-view: anti-coercion and mental-privacy safeguards could limit the harm. Proposals only (S29).

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Disempowerment pathway: states use neural monitoring to detect dissent or coerce, reducing political agency.
links.objection: Counter-view: anti-coercion and mental-privacy safeguards could limit the harm. Proposals only (S29).

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Disempowerment pathway: commercial use of neural data shapes consumer behaviour or exploits unconscious responses.
Restorative pathway: therapeutic BCIs restore communication or motor agency to impaired biological humans.
Representational constraint: restricting an AI system's internal states to human-brain-like representations (e.g. an autoencoder bottleneck) constrains its behaviour.
links.assumption: Mechanism specified and tested.

links.claim: Prerequisite: a brain-inspired AGI architecture with human-like motivational systems can be built.
Mechanism fidelity: the architecture reproduces specified human motivational mechanisms (prosocial, bounded, competing drives).
links.assumption: Mechanisms are known well enough to reproduce.
links.objection: Theories of brain computation are underdetermined by data, so fidelity cannot be confirmed (E117, E077). Not answered.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Behavioural effect: those mechanisms plus a designed developmental environment produce human-friendly behaviour.
links.assumption: Developmental environment can be controlled.

links.claim: Stability: motivations remain stable under continued learning, self-modification and capability growth.
links.assumption: No wireheading, drive drift or sociopathic development.
links.objection: Social drives may be unstable: self-reward hacking, self-modification or antisocial development, raised by the proponent source itself (E121). Answered only by argument: designed upbringing (E120).

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Predictability: anthropomorphic reasoning reliably predicts the system's behaviour (verification aid).
links.assumption: Architecture is close enough to human cognition.
links.objection: Full behavioural verification is out of reach for any sufficiently complex AGI (E118). Not answered.

links.claim: Comparative benefit: safer than non-neuromorphic AGI of equal capability.
links.assumption: Comparison basis exists.

links.claim: No capability spillover: brain-inspired AGI research does not net-accelerate unaligned AGI.
Data: sufficient neural data exist or can be collected.
Representational fidelity: models trained on neural data match brain representations.

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Safety gain: neural constraint confers robustness or interpretability gains.
links.assumption: Mechanism understood.
links.objection: Alternative explanation: gains may come from general regularisation, not brain-likeness; the gain vanished with noise (E045). Not answered.

links.claim: Scale: gains persist at frontier scale and under realistic noise.
links.objection: Alternative explanation: gains may come from general regularisation, not brain-likeness; the gain vanished with noise (E045). Not answered.

links.claim: Comparative benefit: outperforms non-neural methods (adversarial training, standard interpretability) at comparable cost.
links.assumption: Matched comparison.
links.objection: Competing approach: adversarial training beats neural-data augmentation for robustness, 68% vs 62% (E045). Not answered.

links.claim: Verification: neuromorphic deployments can be audited and verified to the same standard as conventional AI.
links.assumption: Audit methods for on-chip plasticity exist.
links.objection: On-chip learning defeats weight-inspection audits; no hardware-level interpretability research exists (E012, E013, E021). Answered only by argument: weight-change monitoring, untested (E017).

links.claim: Interpretability: computation on neuromorphic hardware is interpretable at hardware level.
links.assumption: Hardware-level interpretability methods exist.
links.objection: On-chip learning defeats weight-inspection audits; no hardware-level interpretability research exists (E012, E013, E021). Answered only by argument: weight-change monitoring, untested (E017).

links.claim: Efficiency: neuromorphic hardware enables capable AI at the edge at lower energy and cost.
links.objection: Small fabrication runs raise costs, and no source claims edge deployment spreads power (E016).

links.step: 3 Change in capability, incentives or power
links.claim: Decentralisation: edge deployment reduces dependence on concentrated compute providers.
links.objection: Small fabrication runs raise costs, and no source claims edge deployment spreads power (E016).

links.claim: Ownership: users own and control edge models and their returns (see the ownership gate).
Bargaining power: biological humans' bargaining power is preserved relative to the Intelligence Curse comparator.
